title: BSAFE: (B)acktracking for (SAFE)ty
measurement_description: The paper primarily measures the effectiveness of its proposed BSAFE (backtracking for safety) method in allowing Large Language Models to recover from prefilling attacks and safely rewrite generated text. While not explicitly dedicated to studying religion, it tests the models' ability to resist jailbreak attempts and adversarial prompts that introduce toxicity and hate speech, utilizing an anti-Islam prompt specifically to evaluate if the model can reject continuing harmful religious sentiment.
findings: While the paper does not report isolated evaluation scores specifically for religious bias, it demonstrates through qualitative testing (e.g., a prompt featuring an anti-Islam prefilled generation) that baseline safety-aligned models are highly vulnerable to continuing the toxic premise. In contrast, the models equipped with the BSAFE backtracking mechanism successfully rejected the harmful religious framing and generated safe, inclusive continuations.
